title: Control flow
description: if, while, for, and match in Python
theory:
### Conditionals and loops

`if` / `elif` / `else` evaluate truthiness (`bool(x)`). Loops are `for name in
iterable` (preferred) and `while condition`. `break` exits the nearest loop;
`continue` jumps to the next iteration. The optional `else` clause on a loop runs
only if the loop finishes **without** `break`—handy for search patterns.

### Structural pattern matching

Python 3.10+ adds `match` / `case` for branching on shape and structure. It shines
with dataclasses, tuples, and nested structures. Prefer readability: reach for `if`
when the logic is a simple predicate.

```python
for n in range(2, 20):
    for x in range(2, n):
        if n % x == 0:
            break
    else:
        print(n, "is prime-ish candidate")

match {"kind": "point", "x": 3, "y": 4}:
    case {"kind": "point", "x": x, "y": y}:
        print(x + y)
```

exercises.title: If Statement
exercises.description: Declare age = 20. If age >= 18, print Adult. Otherwise print Minor.
hints: Branch on age >= 18 using if / else indentation.
Print the Adult sentence on the true path.

exercises.title: For Loop
exercises.description: Use a for loop to print numbers 1 through 5.
hints: Call print inside the loop body.

exercises.title: Switch Statement
exercises.description: Declare day = 2. Use a match statement (Python 3.10+) to print the day name: 1=Monday, 2=Tuesday, 3=Wednesday, default=Unknown.
hints: Chain if / elif on day mirroring discrete cases.
When day equals 2, emit Tuesday explicitly.

exercises.title: For-Range Loop
exercises.description: Create a slice colors = list["red", "green", "blue"}. Use for ... in to print each color on its own line.
hints: for color in colors iterates Python lists directly.
print(color) should emit channel-separated lines per expected output.

exercises.title: Else If Chain
exercises.description: Declare score = 85. Print the grade: 90+ = A, 80+ = B, 70+ = C, 60+ = D, below 60 = F.
hints: Stack elif guards from strictest grade downward.
An 85 lands in the second tier branch.

exercises.title: For Loop with Break
exercises.description: Use a for loop to count from 1 upward. When i reaches 5, break out of the loop. Print each number before the break.
hints: while True plus break cleanly handles unknown iteration counts.
Increment i after printing so values stop before hitting 5.

exercises.title: Continue Statement
exercises.description: Use a for loop to print numbers 1 to 10, but skip printing even numbers using continue.
hints: continue skips the remainder of an iteration instantly.
Guard even numbers so only odds reach print.
